README.mdOutline

Security Advisory: Denial of Service in Technitium DNS Server Rate Limiting

Status: Fixed in the latest Technitium DNS Server releases (version 14.0)

Impact: Denial of Service (DoS) against legitimate DNS clients/resolvers

Access Vector: Remote, unauthenticated

CVE: CVE-2025-50334

CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

Published Date (Vendors): 8th November 2025

Affects: Technitium DNS Server up to and including 13.6

Not affected: Technitium DNS Server version 14.0

Impact: Remote Denial of Service against legitimate DNS clients/resolvers via subnet-wide blacklisting

Severity: High

CVSS v3.1: 7.5, see https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln-metrics/cvss/v3-calculator?vector=AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Our team identified a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability in the rate-limiting implementation of Technitium DNS Server.

Under the default configuration, a remote attacker who can spoof source IP addresses can abuse the rate-limiting mechanism to temporarily block legitimate DNS traffic for entire IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /56 subnets.

This issue affects Technitium DNS Server both when it is deployed as a recursive resolver and when it operates as an authoritative name server.

This issue has been fixed in version 14.0. The DNS Server now has a redesigned rate-limiting implementation with different Queries Per Minute (QPM) options in Settings that help mitigate this issue.

Credits

This vulnerability in Technitium DNS Server’s rate-limiting implementation was discovered by:

Shiming Liu, Yunyi Zhang, Ruixuan Li, Baojun Liu, Donghong Sun, and Haixin Duan

Network and Information Security Lab, Tsinghua University.

We thank the Technitium Security Team for their prompt response and collaboration on the proposed mitigations.

Reference

Technitium DNS Server Change Log. https://github.com/TechnitiumSoftware/DnsServer/commit/db379366069e3bb981c0f25c513c0e1b8d065a45
